clue.text: Great works of literature in Latin and Greek

definitions.meaning: books long held up as the finest of their kind, the standard canon
the study of the ancient languages and their literature as a university subject

explanation.surface: A description of the great books written in the two ancient tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both enduring masterpieces and the academic study of ancient Rome and Greece.

clue.text: Rumoured to be the location of atmospheric pollution

definitions.meaning: talked about vaguely and widely, as a feeling that something is coming
literally where smog and fumes are found: up in the sky

explanation.surface: Gossip that smog is somewhere overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a rumour or feeling circulating, and literally where smog hangs, up above the ground.

clue.text: Clamp down on out-of-print publications

parts.note: OP is the bookseller's abbreviation for out of print
the press means newspapers and other publications collectively

explanation.surface: A censor cracking down on books that are no longer available.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to rule harshly and keep people down, a synonym for clamping down.

clue.text: Make certain as certain can be

parts.note: certain and sure are synonyms

explanation.surface: Making doubly sure, as sure as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the saying 'as sure as can be'; 'can be' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure is to guarantee or make sure of something.

clue.text: Where the skill of film production came in

indicators.note: producing something means making it up afresh from raw materials, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A remark about where filmmaking talent first got started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' looks like part of 'film production', but it is the anagram signal working on the letters of CAME IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The picture house is the place where the art of moviemaking is shown and celebrated.

clue.text: Preoccupation with mortification of the flesh

definitions.meaning: a dominant interest or obsession governing someone's life
read literally, controlling or governing one's bodily desires

explanation.surface: An obsession with self-denial and bodily discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a master obsession, and read literally means governing one's bodily desire, as ascetic self-denial does.

clue.text: Alert workers should before going to bed

definitions.meaning: to warn people of danger, as a verb

definitions.text: workers should before going to bed
definitions.meaning: read literally, people with jobs should wind up or set the clock bell before sleeping

explanation.surface: Advice that employees set their clocks before turning in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means giving warning of danger, and playfully what a worker does to an alarm clock at night.

clue.text: A borderline political party

parts.note: read as a party located at a country's border line, punning on a frontier between nations

explanation.surface: A party on the fringes of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: A former British far-right party; 'borderline' suggests both extreme and a frontier between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a fringe British political party, and the name also suggests the boundary of a nation.

clue.text: Pretentious art school which little Christopher tops

indicators.note: one piece sitting on top of or ahead of the other, so the name comes first

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher

explanation.surface: A school of tasteless art headed by a young boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, tasteless or sentimental art is described as kitsch.

clue.text: Way to lodge permit for a gambling game

indicators.note: lodging something means setting it firmly inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a route is a way to go
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Getting a licence to put up a casino game.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino game in which a ball falls into a numbered slot on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Lamb's mother unaffected by reversal

indicators.note: says the word looks the same when written backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A sheep that cannot be turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep, the parent of a young lamb.

clue.text: Education graduate in a great Islamic centre

parts.note: MEd is a Master of Education degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher with a degree studying at a famous Muslim seat of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saudi Arabian holy city where the Prophet is buried, second in importance to Mecca.

clue.text: That woman has to betray one of cabinet fame

parts.note: she refers to a female person
to rat on someone is to betray them

explanation.surface: A woman betraying a government cabinet minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinet' suggests government, but it is furniture: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English cabinetmaker and designer.
explanation.definitionFit: The English designer famous for furniture, including cabinets, in a neoclassical style.

clue.text: No cooked-up bloody conflict

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a war is a bloody conflict

explanation.surface: A war that was not invented.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncooked food is described as raw.

clue.text: They follow one drink with another

definitions.meaning: short drinks taken after another kind, as a whisky after beer

explanation.surface: Drinkers who knock back one drink after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuers are those who follow, and a short drink taken after another is also so called.

clue.text: For instance, nothing is needed for self-esteem

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates for example
the figure zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A remark that self-respect needs nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: One's sense of self-worth is one's ego.

clue.text: What the climber changes out of the climbing motorist changes into

definitions.text: What the climber changes out of the climbing motorist changes into

parts.words: What the climber changes out of the climbing motorist changes into
parts.note: a mountaineer leaves the valley floor behind, while a driver going uphill shifts down to a slow setting of the gearbox

explanation.surface: A riddle contrasting a mountaineer and a driver on a steep road.
explanation.definitionFit: The slowest gearbox setting, used for steep hills, and punningly the low clothing or ground a climber leaves.

clue.text: He looks at a Sunday paper

definitions.meaning: a British national Sunday newspaper of that name

explanation.surface: A man reading his weekend newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a long-established British Sunday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: One who watches, and the title of a British weekend newspaper.

clue.text: A suggestion of some monkey business about a lad leaving home

definitions.text: A suggestion of some monkey business

parts.note: going means departing
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Hints of mischief as a young man moves out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means suspicious or improper activity, the kind of mischief hinted at.

clue.text: Lavish praise on a duke in the obituary column

annotationWithheld.clue: Lavish praise on a duke in the obituary column

clue.text: Time-honoured theatrical director was under an obligation

parts.note: Sir Peter Hall was a famous British theatre director, founder of the Royal Shakespeare Company
owed means was in debt to someone

explanation.surface: A veteran stage director who was in someone's debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means sacred or revered through long tradition.

clue.text: Is a lie contrived just to make contact?

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially made up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Asking whether an invented falsehood is a way to get in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to communicate and cooperate with others.

clue.text: Welsh secretary who sets the pace

definitions.meaning: Peter ... was Secretary of State for Wales in the late 1980s
a person on foot moving at a steady speed

explanation.surface: A government minister leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh Secretary is the British cabinet minister responsible for Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname of a Welsh Secretary, and someone who goes on foot at their own pace.

clue.text: Disdainful Poles afflicted by uncertainty

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
iffy means doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: Polish people made scornful by doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland, but it is the two compass poles. 'Iffy' is an adjective, loosely clued here by a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniffy means scornful and contemptuous, turning up one's nose.

clue.text: Find employment for socially-superior, high-employment area

parts.note: U means upper-class in British usage
SE is the South East of England, a prosperous region with many jobs

explanation.surface: Finding work for a posh person in a booming region.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something is to put it to work.

clue.text: The electrical circuit allowing some latitude

definitions.meaning: a circuit in which components are side by side rather than in series
a line of latitude on a map, running east to west

explanation.surface: A wiring arrangement giving some freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' suggests leeway, but it means a line on the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit with branches side by side, and a line of latitude on the globe.

clue.text: Ignore built-up area

indicators.note: something built up is constructed anew, so the letters are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Advice to overlook an urban district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built-up area' reads as a town, but 'built-up' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is a district or area.

clue.text: Lost opportunity by the nostalgic Chunnel traveller?

definitions.meaning: failed to take a chance while it was there
someone crossing by rail under the Channel who longs for the old ferry

explanation.surface: A rail passenger to France who misses the old ferries.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chunnel is the rail tunnel under the English Channel, which replaced many ferry crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being too late to seize a chance, and literally longing for the cross-Channel ferry.
